related_questions.question: What is the protocol for being exposed to COVID-19?

text_blocks.snippet: If exposed to COVID-19, the main recommendation is to monitor for symptoms, get tested if symptoms develop, and follow public health precautions. Specifically, individuals should watch for symptoms for 14 days and self-quarantine for 10 days from the last contact if asymptomatic. If a test is positive, immediate home isolation and guidance from a healthcare provider are necessary.

list.snippet: Monitor for symptoms: Watch for any symptoms of COVID-19 for 14 days after exposure.
Get tested: If you develop symptoms, get tested for COVID-19.
Follow public health precautions: Continue to follow all public health recommendations, such as wearing a mask, maintaining distance, and practicing good hygiene.
Self-quarantine: If you don't develop symptoms, you should self-quarantine for 10 days from your last contact with the infected person.
End quarantine: You can end quarantine if you remain symptom-free and have had no further contact with someone with COVID-19, and the infected person has completed their isolation.
Contact your doctor: If you have symptoms, contact your healthcare provider.
Isolate if positive: If you test positive, immediately isolate at home and follow the guidance of your healthcare provider.
